land.text: the Turkmen SSR: the Transcaspian Oblast and parts of the Bukharan and Khorezm republics 'unified to create the Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic' in the national delimitation of October 1924; 'a separate republic of the USSR as the Turkmen SSR' on 13 May 1925; 'Since its creation, the borders of Soviet Turkmenistan remained unchanged'

predecessors.note: 'Turkmenistan declared its independence on 27 October 1991'; the Supreme Soviet had declared sovereignty on 22 August 1990; 'On 26 December 1991, the Soviet Union ceased to exist.' Cliopatria's row starts in 1992 (source for the predecessor land: the Turkmen SSR page).

correction.text: the Turkmen SSR's territory, independent from 27 October 1991

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: independence was declared on 27 October 1991, two months before the Soviet Union 'ceased to exist' on 26 December; Cliopatria's row starts in 1992. The 1992 outline is used for 1991 and overlaps the USSR's last year. The page words the declaration as 'following the dissolution of the Soviet Union' although its date precedes the dissolution; the dates are kept.

467,932 km2 against the infobox 491,210 km2 (body text 488,100 km2): ratio 0.95 to 0.96. On the grid the outline has 1,625 cells, 1,604 of them inside Natural Earth's Turkmenistan; 21 lie outside it (10 in Uzbekistan, 4 in Afghanistan, 7 elsewhere) and 32 Turkmen cells (about 8,000 km2, spread along the frontier) are left out, edge noise on a frontier the pages record as unchanged since the Soviet republic's creation ('Since its creation, the borders of Soviet Turkmenistan remained unchanged', Turkmen SSR page). One outline for 1992-2023; the page names no border treaty or exchange after 1991 (it gives only 'a series of bilateral treaties' with Uzbekistan in 2004, no terms).
Identical to 1992 on the grid; no territorial change is recorded on the pages opened ('Any change in Turkmenistan's territory since 1991' is not on the Turkmenistan page).

region.text: the Turkmen SSR within its Soviet-era borders, capital Ashgabat

ledger.note: 27 October 1991: Turkmenistan declares its independence. 'Turkmenistan declared its independence on 27 October 1991, following the dissolution of the Soviet Union' (the page's wording; the USSR 'ceased to exist' on 26 December 1991); the constitutional law of that day, Article 1, set the name 'Turkmenistan'. Sovereignty had been declared on 22 August 1990.

certainty.note: The frontiers are the Soviet republic lines of the 1924 delimitation, 'unchanged' since (Turkmen SSR page); the page gives no treaty for the Kazakh, Uzbek, Iranian or Afghan frontiers, so they are sharp as administrative lines. The exception is the Caspian shore, whose legal status the Turkmenistan page does not discuss.

sources.title: Turkmenistan
sources.note: Independence 27 October 1991, name, capital, area 491,210 km2 (infobox) and 488,100 km2 (text), presidents, neighbours. Silent on border treaties (except the 2004 Uzbek treaties, no terms) and on any territorial change since 1991.

sources.title: Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 1924 national delimitation, 13 May 1925 republic, 'borders remained unchanged', sovereignty 22 August 1990. Used for the predecessor land.

notes: Turkmenistan, two identical Cliopatria shapes (1992-2023 and 2024), start moved to 27 October 1991 with a new 1991 keyframe; no territorial event exists after 1991 on the two pages opened (page budget 2 reached). Not opened: the Turkmenistan–Uzbekistan border (treaties of 2004 are named without terms on the Turkmenistan page), the Kazakh, Iranian and Afghan frontiers, the Caspian status and the Amu Darya line; a gap-filler may find small exchanges there. The Taliban neighbour (1996-2001) is a border neighbour only; no territory changed hands. Turkmen SSR page confirms the borders 'remained unchanged' from 1924/1925. The end year is 2024 as in the neighbouring dossiers (Cliopatria's last year).
